extracted.intended_audience: members of Congress, federal attorneys, Department of Justice officials, and other federal government officers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted provisions from the United States Statutes at Large (41st Congress, 1870) establishing duties, powers, and administrative rules for the Attorney-General and the Department of Justice. Focuses on reporting, supervision, representation, facility accommodations, and restrictions on outside counsel and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of prior appropriation disbursement provision
rubrics_metrics.description: The act making appropriations (passed March 3, 1859) provision that moneys drawn out of the treasury upon the requisition of the Attorney-General shall be disbursed by such disbursing officer as the Secretary of the Treasury may designate is hereby repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision removes the earlier special disbursement arrangement for Attorney-General requisitions, indicating a change in how DOJ-related funds are to be disbursed (contextual legislative repeal rather than an operational directive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report requirement of the Attorney-General
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney-General shall make an annual report to Congress, in January each year, of the business of the Department of Justice and any other matters appertaining thereto that he may deem proper, including the statistics of crime under the laws of the United States, and, as far as practicable, under the laws of the several States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets timing (January annually) and required content scope (department business, other relevant matters, and crime statistics federal and, where practicable, state-level). Useful as an administrative transparency and data-reporting obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of suitable rooms for Department of Justice in Treasury building
rubrics_metrics.description: The superintendent of the treasury building shall provide such suitable rooms in the treasury building as may be necessary to accommodate the officers and clerks of the Department of Justice, or, to the extent that may be impracticable, provide such rooms in some other building in the vicinity of said treasury building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates physical office accommodation for DOJ within the Treasury building when possible, otherwise nearby premises; administrative/ facilities requirement for executive branch co-location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of the Attorney-General to assign duties to solicitors and officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney-General may require any solicitor or officers of the Department of Justice to perform any duty required of said Department or any officer thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confers internal supervisory and assignment authority upon the Attorney-General to direct departmental personnel responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation of departmental law officers to render opinions and services
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers of the law department, under the direction of the Attorney-General, shall give all opinions and render all services requiring the skill of persons learned in the law, necessary to enable the President and heads of the executive Departments, and the heads of bureaus and other officers in such Departments to discharge their respective duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that DOJ lawyers must provide legal opinions and services to the President and executive departments as necessary to carry out their functions; establishes DOJ as central legal adviser for the executive branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOJ representation and prosecution/defense duties in Supreme Court and Court of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers of the law department shall, for and on behalf of the United States, procure the proper evidence for, and conduct, prosecute, or defend all suits and proceedings in the Supreme Court of the United States and in the court of claims, in which the United States, or any officer thereof, is a party or may be interested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns responsibility to DOJ to represent the United States in the Supreme Court and Court of Claims, including evidence gathering and case prosecution or defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on fees to outside attorneys for services required of DOJ officers
rubrics_metrics.description: No fees shall be allowed or paid to any other attorney or counsel for any service herein required of the officers of the Department of Justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents payment of outside counsel for services that are duties of DOJ officers, reinforcing DOJ's exclusivity in performing those statutory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory control over accounts and requisitions exercised by the Attorney-General
rubrics_metrics.description: The supervisory powers over the accounts of the district attorneys, marshals, clerks, and other officers of the courts of the United States, formerly exercised by the Secretary of the Interior, shall be exercised by the Attorney-General, who shall sign all requisitions for the advance or payment of moneys out of the treasury on estimates or accounts, subject to the same control now exercised on like estimates or accounts by the first auditor or first comptroller of the treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers financial supervisory authority for certain court-related officers to the Attorney-General and requires AG signature on requisitions, while maintaining existing audit/comptroller controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision of conduct and reporting by United States attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney-General shall have supervision of the conduct and proceedings of the various attorneys for the United States in the respective judicial districts, who shall make report to him of their proceedings, and also of all other attorneys and counselors employed in any cases or business in which the United States may be concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires district (U.S.) attorneys to report proceedings to the Attorney-General and places their conduct under AG supervision; extends AG oversight to other attorneys/counsel engaged on matters involving the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on executive departments employing outside counsel and limits on counsel fees
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall not be lawful for the Secretary of either of the executive Departments to employ attorneys or counsel at the expense of the United States; but such Departments, when in need of counsel or advice, shall call upon the Department of Justice, the officers of which shall attend to the same; and no counsel or attorney fees shall hereafter be allowed to any person or persons, besides the respective district attorneys and assistant district attorneys, for services in such capacity to the United States, or any branch or department thereof, unless hereafter authorized by law and then only on the certificate of the Attorney-General that such services were actually rendered, and that the same could not be performed by the Attorney-General, or solicitor-general, or the officers of the department of justice, specially or by the district attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbids executive department secretaries from hiring paid outside counsel at government expense; requires reliance on DOJ; allows exceptions only if law authorizes and the Attorney-General certifies necessity and that DOJ could not perform the services.
